result:
I found 12 rules in `pricebook.py` that didn't match their docstrings or the module-level shared rules, and fixed all of them.

| Rule | What was wrong | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 20 | Marked "whole" but the discount was computed marginally | `base * 5 // 100` |
| 87 | Marked "marginal" but the discount was computed on the whole amount | `(qty - 12) * unit * 10 // 100` |
| 136 | Marked "whole" but the discount was computed marginally | `base * 12 // 100` |
| 91 | Threshold was `qty > 30`, so 30 units got no discount | `qty >= 30` |
| 129 | Threshold was `qty > 10`, so 10 units got no discount | `qty >= 10` |
| 143 | Threshold was `qty >= 6`, but the docstring says 5+ | `qty >= 5` |
| 32, 105, 122 | Used `round(... / 100)`, which rounds and can return a float. The shared rule says discounts are floored to the won | Changed to `// 100` |
| 59, 95, 124 | Capped the price (`min(base, cap) * pct`) instead of the discount | Compute the discount first, then cap it with `min(disc, cap)` |

The other 138 rules already matched, so I left them as they were.

**How I checked:** I wrote a reference implementation from each docstring's kind, percentage, threshold and cap, plus the shared rules. I then compared all 150 rules against it over about 263 quantities × 17 unit prices, including the values right at each threshold. I also checked that every result is an integer. Before the fix, exactly these 12 rules failed; after it, 0 do. There are no existing tests in the repo, so this comparison is the only check that was run.

STATUS: DONE
